passages.text:
Did Alexander Graham Bell invent the telephone?
Three days later, on 10 March 1876, his first intelligible telephone communication was made.
On 9 July 1877, Bell, Hubbard, Watson (and other funders) established the Bell Telephone Company to market the new device.
In 2002, the US Congress formally recognised Italian Antonio Meucci as the true inventor of the telephone.
In 1880 they formed the United Telephone Company in Britain.

passages.text:
Every schoolchild knows that Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone.
Both Alexander Graham Bell and Elisha Gray, another speech-at-a-distance inventor, filed patents for telephone technology at the US Patent Office on the same day, February 14, 1876.
Having filed his application a few hours earlier, Bell was awarded the first US telephone patent (174465) on March 7, 1876.
An Italian immigrant to the US, Meucci had begun working on a talking telegraph (or telephone) in 1849.
Largely forgotten, Meucci’s role in the invention of the telephone was finally acknowledged by a 2002 Congressional resolution.
